title: AION audit: Red Sea optionality is state-dependent, not directional alpha
net_new_delta: Historical same-regime evidence shows Bab el-Mandeb threat realizations can produce measurable traffic rerouting and freight costs, but the new Saudi offensive-preparation report is a two-sided transition whose near-term directional market sign is unidentified. Treat preparation, execution, traffic response, and physical-flow response as separate states.

evidence.finding: Five tankers changed course after Houthi threats; Reuters estimated rerouting could add about 10,000 nautical miles, 34 sailing days, more than $5m freight excluding fuel/insurance, plus about $1m Suez transit per vessel.
Bab el-Mandeb commodity-vessel crossings fell to 11, the lowest in months, after Houthi attacks; physical crude cargo prices rose to two-month highs.
Saudi Arabia is preparing a Yemeni-led offensive around Bab el-Mandeb; timing and success remain uncertain.

maturity_change: Causal state decomposition advances; no model, parameter, anomaly-predictiveness, calibration, or performance maturity increase.
blockers: No ablation separating threat, traffic, freight, physical-flow and concurrent Hormuz effects
next_decisive_experiment: Preregister Red Sea episodes with preparation->execution->attack/retaliation->traffic/rerouting->freight/insurance->physical-flow states. Compare state-only, traffic, and flow models at frozen horizons; cluster by episode, correct the full test family, ablate concurrent Hormuz shocks, and reserve the final contiguous episode block untouched for OOS. Only then test trading costs.

aion.finding: Durable causal memory should encode Red Sea preparation, execution, traffic response and physical-flow response separately; historical rerouting proves the transmission channel exists but not the sign of the new preparation event.

ascension.finding: The new event has exact Git provenance and external corroboration, but neither independence, multiplicity, OOS nor directional performance authority is established.

prometheus.finding: Prioritize a state-transition event study with traffic/flow ablations over headline-direction inference; preserve negative and ambiguous episodes.
